# Sensor replacement (cam, crank, O2, MAF)

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Replace the leaking rocker cover gasket and swap in a new O2 sensor. [t69]

Replace the rock-hard PCV blowby hose. [t69]

[Partial] Dismantle the entire reservoir unit to access internal components. [t77]

[Partial] Locate, remove, and replace both cam position sensors on the valve covers. [t327]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Replace the leaking rocker cover gasket to stop oil from saturating sensor wires.
2. [Partial] Swap in a new O2 sensor, preferably an NTK or Denso brand for longevity.

_Procedure reported by [t69]._

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t77] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Dismantle the entire reservoir unit to access internal components.
2. [Partial] Check if the float is stuck inside.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t327] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Locate the cam position sensors on the valve covers.
2. [Partial] Remove and replace both sensors as preventative maintenance while other parts are off.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t69] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Replace the rock-hard PCV blowby hose to ensure proper airflow and prevent pressure issues.

</details>

## Parts

- [Partial] Aftermarket washer fluid kit [t77]

## Tips & gotchas

- Note that standalone sensors are rare; kits often include the reservoir, pump, and sensor. [t77]
- Check for small leaks at the back of the passenger side where these sit. [t327]
